input: s1, s2 and baseStr contain only ASCII lowercase letters. s1 and s2 have equal length n; baseStr has length m. Empty strings are allowed. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. JavaScript integers are primitive safe-integer Number values, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Lexicographically smallest string equivalent to baseStr under the reflexive/symmetric/transitive relation generated by s1[i] equivalent to s2[i]. Every character is replaced by the smallest letter in its component.
mutation_aliasing: All input strings remain unchanged. The disjoint-set arrays, output characters and returned string are private/new; the Solution object retains no state.
numeric: Alphabet indices lie in [0, 25]; component counts/sizes at most 26; character-code arithmetic remains in ASCII. Positions are bounded by n and m. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n + m + 1) time because the disjoint-set universe is fixed at 26, with O(m + 1) auxiliary/output space including output characters and joined result. The full union-find helper, including unused components state, is charged. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.

helpers.name: DisjointSet
helpers.contract: Owns disjoint components of indices 0 through count - 1. find performs path halving; union links smaller size below larger size, maintains the minimum original index at each current root, and decreases components only when two different roots merge. No input-owned array is referenced.
helpers.cost: Initialization O(count + 1) time/space; amortized inverse-Ackermann find/union time over a sequence, O(log(count + 1)) worst-case per operation from union-by-size. Three full arrays and all methods are included even when a client does not read minimum or components. The byte-identical class is fully charged in both clients.
